label: STOPP C5: antiplatelet plus anticoagulant in stable artery disease
title: Antiplatelet with an anticoagulant in stable artery disease
statement: Antiplatelet agents with vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors in patients with stable coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral arterial disease (no evidence of added benefit from dual therapy).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: Combining an antiplatelet with an anticoagulant can increase bleeding. Review the reason for both medicines in stable arterial disease. Low-dose rivaroxaban with aspirin can reduce cardiovascular events in selected people with coronary or peripheral artery disease.

medicine_groups.name: Antiplatelet medicines
medicine_groups.note: Aspirin counts only as a low dose taken daily as an antiplatelet, for example 100 mg. Aspirin used only for pain does not count. A prescribed fraction of a higher-strength tablet counts when the dose and directions support daily antiplatelet use. Asasantin SR is aspirin with dipyridamole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. CoPlavix and DuoCover contain clopidogrel with aspirin. DuoPlidogrel, Piax Plus Aspirin and APX-Clopidogrel/Aspirin 75/100 each contain clopidogrel and aspirin.

medicine_groups.name: Warfarin, dabigatran and the factor Xa inhibitors
medicine_groups.note: Warfarin is the vitamin K antagonist. Dabigatran is the direct thrombin inhibitor. Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban and fondaparinux are factor Xa inhibitors. No Australian brand is listed for edoxaban. Fondaparinux is an injection. Heparin and enoxaparin are not in this group. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 or older. If age is under 65, there is no finding. If age is unknown, request the age before confirming a finding. Suspect a finding when a Group A medicine (an antiplatelet) and a Group B medicine (an anticoagulant) are both supplied, their supply dates overlap or fall within 60 days of each other, and the record shows stable coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral arterial disease during the combined supplies; cite both supplies and the clinical line documenting stability in that period. If the disease history during combined treatment is missing or explicitly unknown, report a possible finding and name that missing fact. If disease is recorded but stability is unclear, report a possible finding. Ask when the last acute event or intervention occurred and whether the disease was stable during combined treatment. The pharmacist judges borderline timing. Documented unstable disease or an explicit negative history gives no C5 finding. If aspirin is the only candidate antiplatelet, calculate its daily dose from strength and directions, including any prescribed tablet fraction. Ask the pharmacist to judge a borderline dose. If daily antiplatelet use is unclear and the other checks allow a finding, report only a possible finding and ask what dose is taken each day and why. Exclude documented use for pain alone.

needs_facts.what: Stable coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral arterial disease
needs_facts.meets: The record documents stable coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral arterial disease during the combined supplies. If disease is recorded but stability is unclear, report a possible finding and ask about a recent acute event or intervention. Documented unstable disease or an explicit negative history gives no C5 finding.

options.words: Arterial disease was stable during combined treatment
Arterial disease was unstable throughout combined treatment
No coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral arterial disease during combined treatment

cannot_be_seen: Whether the arterial disease is stable, why each medicine was started, and any stent or recent heart event not recorded here. Also supplies from a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether the antiplatelet is still needed alongside the anticoagulant.
